**Observations on test image:**
- Severe wilting/drooping of leaves, hanging limply downward
- Leaves remain green — no spots, lesions, or interveinal necrosis visible
- The entire upper canopy of the plant is collapsing
- Some leaf crinkle/puckering texture
- No lesions, pustules, or fungal growth visible

**Reasoning:**
The key feature is **dramatic green wilting** — the plant collapses while leaves remain green. This "flag wilt" pattern is the hallmark of **Sudden Death Syndrome (SDS)** in soybean. In early stages, SDS causes abrupt wilting of green tissue as root rot from *Fusarium virguliforme* interrupts water uptake. The Phytophthora reference showed more advanced browning and stem rot, inconsistent with this green wilt stage. No lesions, spots, or discoloration rule out most foliar diseases (Cercospora, Frogeye, Bacterial Blight, etc.).
